title: Welcome To The Jungle Roars to ₹95 Crore Worldwide in Three Days — Akshay Kumar's Best Opening Since Bhooth Bangla
excerpt: A ₹26-crore Sunday, near-₹100-crore global total, and families pouring in: the opening weekend verdict is in, and the Welcome franchise just proved it still owns the room.
body:
The numbers are in, and they're wearing a Hawaiian shirt.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw</youtube>

**Welcome To The Jungle** — the third instalment of Bollywood's most beloved comedy franchise — has closed its opening weekend at an estimated **₹95 crore worldwide**, falling just ₹5 crore short of the century mark in three days flat. In India alone, the film collected **₹65 crore nett** (₹78 crore gross), while overseas territories chipped in approximately **₹17 crore gross**.

For **Akshay Kumar**, this is the strongest opening since **Bhooth Bangla** earlier this year, and a decisive answer to anyone who'd written off the comedy-entertainer space as a relic of a pre-OTT era.

## Sunday Was the Day It Clicked

The real story of this weekend was Day 3. After a decent but unspectacular Thursday opening of around ₹13 crore nett and a Saturday that nudged past ₹15 crore, Sunday exploded.

By 11 AM on Day 3, the film had already collected ₹4.75 crore nett — up **101 per cent** from the same time slot on Friday and **69 per cent** from Saturday. Morning occupancy jumped from 11 per cent (Day 1) to 12 per cent (Day 2) to **18.23 per cent** (Day 3). By evening, occupancy in several centres crossed 50 per cent.

The final Day 3 estimate: somewhere between **₹26 crore and ₹27 crore nett** — comfortably the film's highest single-day collection and the kind of Sunday surge that tells you families showed up.

> The jump was visible throughout the day. After clocking 40 per cent plus occupancy in the afternoon shows, the film saw evening shows rising to 50 per cent plus occupancy across several centres. — Bollywood Hungama

## Who's Watching and Where

**Maharashtra, Gujarat, and NCR** — the holy trinity of Bollywood comedy — together contributed nearly 50 per cent of the Sunday collections. Among individual cities, **Mumbai** led the charge, followed by **Delhi** and **Ahmedabad**. Pune, which had quietly been outperforming Bengaluru since opening day, continued its strong run.

National chains PVRInox and Cinepolis accounted for 48 per cent of Day 3 collections, while the remaining balance came from mass centres and non-chain properties. That split is key: it means the film is working in both multiplexes and single screens, which is exactly the dual-audience play a Welcome film needs to make.

On **BookMyShow**, Welcome To The Jungle was the clear Bollywood leader, comfortably outpacing both *Main Vaapas Aaunga* and *Cocktail 2* in real-time ticket sales, with peak-hour sales touching **35,990 tickets per hour**.

## The Franchise Math

For context: the original *Welcome* (2007) collected ₹52.47 crore lifetime in India. *Welcome Back* (2015) managed ₹95 crore lifetime. Welcome To The Jungle has nearly matched its predecessor's *entire* run in three days — and with significantly higher ticket prices, the comparison isn't perfectly apples-to-apples, but the trajectory is undeniable.

The bigger question now is legs. The film faces serious competition in the coming weeks: **Alpha** (Alia Bhatt, YRF Spy Universe) arrives July 3, **Dhamaal 4** lands July 10, and Christopher Nolan's **The Odyssey** takes over IMAX screens on July 17. The Monday hold will be crucial — if the film can stay above ₹8-9 crore on its first weekday, a ₹125-crore India nett finish is very much on the table.

## The Ensemble Did Its Job

Director **Ahmed Khan** assembled a cast that reads like a Bollywood comedy fantasy roster: **Akshay Kumar**, **Suniel Shetty**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Raveena Tandon**, **Lara Dutta**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**, **Tusshar Kapoor**, **Shreyas Talpade**, **Aftab Shivdasani**, and **Jackie Shroff**. That's not a cast — that's an attendance sheet from a 2000s Bollywood awards show.

The treatment leans more into spoof and parody than the warm family-entertainer tone of the first two films, which has split opinion among critics and audiences. But the box office doesn't lie: in a month that has seen everything from Imtiaz Ali's quiet magic (*Main Vaapas Aaunga*) to Shahid Kapoor's romantic swagger (*Cocktail 2*), it's the big, loud, deliberately ridiculous comedy that is packing cinemas on a Sunday afternoon.

## Where to Watch — For Now, Theatres Only

Welcome To The Jungle is currently a **theatrical exclusive** across India and worldwide. The film is in wide release in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East. No OTT date has been announced — though given the Netflix deal for *Bhooth Bangla*, expect digital rights to command a premium once the theatrical run concludes.

For diaspora audiences who missed the opening weekend, the film's Monday-to-Thursday hold will determine how long it stays on big screens internationally before Alpha inevitably claims those showtimes.
